entries.old: Kind is immutable. Simple Host: set preset (public, inbox, wall, comments, records, personal, board, private; default private) with optional single-action overrides read, add, edit, delete, or preset custom with all four. Each action takes nobody, owner, own, signed-in or anyone; add also takes checked (anyone who passes the Cloudflare Turnstile spam check: the comments preset, read anyone / add checked / edit owner / delete owner). The server refuses (400 invalid_access, with rule) edit or delete anyone (anonymous_change), add own (add_own), own anywhere with add anyone or checked (own_needs_sign_in), checked on read, edit or delete (checked_add_only), and edit or delete wider than read (change_wider_than_read). checked is refused on files resources, and with 400 spam_check_unavailable on a server without TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and a secret (Simple Hack included). approve_first (SQLite, needs a checked add) holds posts added through the check: the server adds approved_at TEXT to those tables (rows already there count as approved), visitors see and reach only rows with approved_at set, and the owner approves with UPDATE ... SET approved_at = datetime('now'). Omit approve_first to keep it. SQLite: the preset is the database default; tables sets a preset per table (omit to keep the current table presets, {} to clear). Tables whose preset uses own or lets visitors add get the server-owned visitor_id TEXT column and index. The older read, write and write_mode are still accepted and translated (write anyone with full is refused as anonymous_change; omitting write_mode on update keeps the mode); do not mix them with preset fields. Switching a legacy SQLite database pages wrote with SQL to a preset that uses own needs empty tables (visitor_id_required). Owner here means the owner's tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor sign-in; nobody means the owner's tools only. Simple Hack accepts only read and write (anyone, signed-in, owner) with full mode, as before presets.

SET approved_at = datetime('now'). Omit approve_first to keep it. SQLite: the preset is the database default; tables sets a preset per table (omit to keep the current table presets, {} to clear). Tables whose preset uses own or lets visitors add get the server-owned visitor_id TEXT column and index. The older read, write and write_mode are still accepted and translated (write anyone with full is refused as anonymous_change; omitting write_mode on update keeps the mode); do not mix them with preset fields. Switching a legacy SQLite database pages wrote with SQL to a preset that uses own needs empty tables (visitor_id_required). Owner here means the owner's tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor sign-in; nobody means the owner's tools only. Simple Hack accepts only read and write (anyone, signed-in, owner) with full mode, as before presets. With STORAGE_RULES=on, SQLite and SQLite-stored KV resources also accept rules (StoragePolicySet), without preset fields. A rules save on a Postgres KV namespace returns 400 rules_unavailable. Rules are unavailable on file buckets (400 invalid_rules). A body or table rules field with the flag off returns 400 rules_unavailable. Bodies over 256 KiB return 400 invalid_rules with clause size. Null rules are treated as absent; an empty policies array denies visitors. For SQLite, table rules override the default set; omit tables to keep overrides, or send tables {} to clear them. When moving from per-table presets, send rules for every override or tables {}. Preset fields and rules on the same body or table entry return 400 invalid_rules. A rules resource saved back to presets with table overrides requires explicit tables (otherwise 409 tables_present). A passcode-only save on a rules resource preserves rules. Rules responses omit preset fields and carry rules, rules_status and rules_errors. Preset responses remain unchanged with the flag off; with it on they also carry rules_status preset.

Owner here means the owner's tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor sign-in; nobody means the owner's tools only. "description": "Kind is immutable. Simple Host: set preset (public, inbox, wall, comments, records, personal, board, private; default private) with optional single-action overrides read, add, edit, delete, or preset custom with all four. Each action takes nobody, owner, own, signed-in or anyone; add also takes checked (anyone who passes the Cloudflare Turnstile spam check: the comments preset, read anyone / add checked / edit owner / delete owner). The server refuses (400 invalid_access, with rule) edit or delete anyone (anonymous_change), add own (add_own), own anywhere with add anyone or checked (own_needs_sign_in), checked on read, edit or delete (checked_add_only), and edit or delete wider than read (change_wider_than_read). checked is refused on files resources, and with 400 spam_check_unavailable on a server without TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and a secret (Simple Hack included). approve_first (SQLite, needs a checked add) holds posts added through the check: the server adds approved_at TEXT to those tables (rows already there count as approved), visitors see and reach only rows with approved_at set, and the owner approves with UPDATE ... SET approved_at = datetime('now'). Omit approve_first to keep it. SQLite: the preset is the database default; tables sets a preset per table (omit to keep the current table presets, {} to clear). Tables whose preset uses own or lets visitors add get the server-owned visitor_id TEXT column and index. The older read, write and write_mode are still accepted and translated (write anyone with full is refused as anonymous_change; omitting write_mode on update keeps the mode); do not mix them with preset fields. Switching a legacy SQLite database pages wrote with SQL to a preset that uses own needs empty tables (visitor_id_required). Owner here means the owner's tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor sign-in; nobody means the owner's tools only. Simple Hack accepts only read and write (anyone, signed-in, owner) with full mode, as before presets. With STORAGE_RULES=on, SQLite and SQLite-stored KV resources also accept rules (StoragePolicySet), without preset fields. A rules save on a Postgres KV namespace returns 400 rules_unavailable. Rules are unavailable on file buckets (400 invalid_rules). A body or table rules field with the flag off returns 400 rules_unavailable. Bodies over 256 KiB return 400 invalid_rules with clause size. Null rules are treated as absent; an empty policies array denies visitors. For SQLite, table rules override the default set; omit tables to keep overrides, or send tables {} to clear them. When moving from per-table presets, send rules for every override or tables {}. Preset fields and rules on the same body or table entry return 400 invalid_rules. A rules resource saved back to presets with table overrides requires explicit tables (otherwise 409 tables_present). A passcode-only save on a rules resource preserves rules. Rules responses omit preset fields and carry rules, rules_status and rules_errors. Preset responses remain unchanged with the flag off; with it on they also carry rules_status preset.",

Owner here means the owner's tools and the owner signed in on the site's own address through visitor sign-in; nobody means the owner's tools only. Simple Hack accepts only read and write (anyone, signed-in, owner) with full mode, as before presets.

With STORAGE_RULES=on, SQLite and SQLite-stored KV resources also accept rules (StoragePolicySet), without preset fields. A rules save on a Postgres KV namespace returns 400 rules_unavailable. Rules are unavailable on file buckets (400 invalid_rules). A body or table rules field with the flag off returns 400 rules_unavailable. Bodies over 256 KiB return 400 invalid_rules with clause size. Null rules are treated as absent; an empty policies array denies visitors. For SQLite, table rules override the default set; omit tables to keep overrides, or send tables {} to clear them. When moving from per-table presets, send rules for every override or tables {}. Preset fields and rules on the same body or table entry return 400 invalid_rules. A rules resource saved back to presets with table overrides requires explicit tables (otherwise 409 tables_present). A passcode-only save on a rules resource preserves rules. Rules responses omit preset fields and carry rules, rules_status and rules_errors. Preset responses remain unchanged with the flag off; with it on they also carry rules_status preset.
